batch_sizing.note: Reference servings are batches of the SAME SIZE as the mixed batch, differing only in composition: the request under test keeps its own prompt, selection and row position, and every other row is unsteered filler carrying no selection. BATCH-SIZE-1 (SOLO) REFERENCES ARE INVALID ON THIS ENGINE AND HARDWARE AND MUST NOT BE REINSTATED. Measured on vLLM 0.25.1 / H200 (SM90) in job 173152, and reproduced on a bare engine with no steering code and vllm-lens not installed: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 does not deliver batch-size-1-versus-N bit-invariance. Batch sizes 6, 7, 8, 11, 15 and 16 agreed bit-exactly with each other; batch size 1 differed, flipping a single near-tie token mid-generation, because the flag's SM90 path installs cuBLAS workspace configs rather than shape-pinned matmul kernels and a residual kernel still varies with M. Comparing a batched row against a solo serving therefore reports cross-request contamination that is not there: it did exactly that in job 173152, whose batched outputs were bit-perfect, and cost a debugging cycle. For the same reason every row of a size-fixed batch is pinned to the full token budget with ignore_eos, so the running batch cannot shrink toward small M in one composition and not the other.

exact_replay_dropped: EXACT REPLAY IS DROPPED (the user's decision, 2026-08-27): the audit serves serving_mode=interleaved with no VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT, so RE-RUNNING THE AUDIT WILL NOT REPRODUCE ITS TRANSCRIPTS BIT-FOR-BIT — a request's output may vary with the composition of the batch it happens to share. That is a real reduction of the artifact's guarantee, accepted knowingly because what BI=1 actually bought was weaker than advertised: 2.97x throughput for SAME-SIZE composition invariance only (H200/SM90 never had batch-size-1-versus-N invariance, job 173152), on a serving path whose live batch size fluctuates continuously. What IS still certified at the production configuration: repeat-determinism (same batch submitted twice is byte-identical), scale-0 no-op, steering-bites per arm, and DIRECT selection routing (the worker's own record of which object it bound). fidelity_phases.expected_failure_reason: EXPECTED AT VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0, NOT A REGRESSION. batch_invariance and selection_honored each compare one request's output across two DIFFERENT BATCH COMPOSITIONS — its row in the mixed batch against its row in a same-size reference batch whose other members are unsteered filler. Composition invariance is exactly what VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 provides on this stack, so removing it can move those outputs for purely numerical reasons with nothing wrong in the serving path. A failure of these two at BI=0 therefore says the flag was doing something, not that the serving path broke; the BI=1 phase in the same record is the verdict on the serving path. The checks that do NOT depend on composition — engine_determinism (the same batch submitted twice), scale0_noop and steering_bites (same-composition comparisons) — are expected to hold at BI=0, and a failure of any of THEM is a real finding. selection_honored additionally carries a DIRECT half (selection_direct) that does not depend on outputs at all, so when the output half fails here the direct half says whether routing was still correct.
fidelity_phases.headline: REPEAT-DETERMINISM is the headline at BI=0, and it is a different and weaker property than batch invariance: same prompts, same batch composition, same order, submitted twice, byte-identical output. BI governs invariance ACROSS compositions; engine_determinism measures it WITHIN one. Production (serving_mode=interleaved, no VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT) depends on repeat-determinism and NOT on composition invariance — the consuming lane's chunking is deterministic by construction and its bar is aggregate agreement with a reported divergence rate, not byte-identity — which is why engine_determinism GATES at BI=0 while batch_invariance is waived (EXACT_REPLAY_DROPPED_NOTE). If engine_determinism does NOT hold at BI=0, that is the headline finding and it fails the job: any downstream equivalence gate that compares generations byte-for-byte would be passing on luck.

selection_direct.arm_status: armed: the worker's selection record was reset
selection_direct.note: THE DIRECT HALF of selection_honored, and it does not replace the output-comparison half — both are reported, because they answer different questions and disagreement between them is itself informative. The gate's own selection_honored check concludes the right object was loaded because the output looks like that arm's output; that inference is sound only while outputs are composition-stable, which is what VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 was providing. This half instead reads the worker's OWN record of which object it resolved and bound for each request, so it holds at either BI setting. Read the pair together: direct passes and output fails = the right objects were loaded and the outputs moved for numerical reasons (expected at BI=0); direct FAILS = a real routing bug, which outranks everything else in this record; both pass = the strongest form of the claim. The worker record ships its own `coverage` string stating what it does not cover — notably op-level mis-binding downstream of selection, which would read as a clean pass here. ONE UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION, and it degrades loudly rather than silently: the PER-ROW half correlates a submitted row to the worker's record through RequestOutput.request_id, which should equal the id in the runner's input_batch but has never been checked on hardware. If it does not hold, every selected row comes back `unobserved` and the verdict is MISSING — never a pass — while the AGGREGATE half (every observation the worker made bound what was asked for, plus the set of cells actually resolved) still applies, because it needs no correlation at all.

worker_record.coverage: WHAT THIS OBSERVES. At the APPLY SITE, per request per steered layer, the identity of the LoadedObject the slot carries — the object WorkerObjectRegistry.select RESOLVED for that request's selector, READ rather than re-derived — plus whether applying it actually modified that request's rows at that layer. So it is a DIRECT observation of routing: which cell id, which expect_hash and which effective_scale the worker bound to each request, compared against what the request asked for. effective_scale plus n_applications_modifying is the cheap check that a scale-0 twin was not served in place of its live arm or the reverse: a twin must carry scale 0.0 and modify nothing, an arm must carry its serving scale and modify something. WHAT IT DOES NOT OBSERVE, stated plainly rather than left to be assumed. (1) OP-LEVEL BINDING: that the ops fired were computed from the right tensors is not measured, so a mis-binding DOWNSTREAM of selection — correct cell id resolved, wrong tensors bound — reads as a clean pass here. (2) registry.apply's own internal re-resolution: apply resolves the same selector against the same immutable registry and therefore returns this same object, but that is an argument about the registry, not something this record measures. Read it as 'routing and binding IDENTITY were correct', never as 'the right math ran'. WHICH APPLY PATH: each observation is also counted under the path that made it — n_applications_per_slot / n_applications_grouped (and the _modifying twins): per_slot = the per-request loop (prefill slots, objects forced per row, everything under SISTEER_LENS_PER_ROW_APPLY=1), grouped = one apply for a vectorized group of decode rows (shadow-verified or not). Record-level only, so a request's entry reads the same on either path; an observation whose caller named no path is counted in n_applications_unattributed, which a reader must treat as a missing attribution, never as either path.
worker_record.note: DIRECT per-request selection evidence, recorded by the worker as it served. It is the observed half of selection_honored; comparing output token ids between compositions is the inferred half, and the two answer different questions. Observation only: nothing on the apply path reads this back, and recording it cannot raise (any internal error is counted in n_record_errors instead of propagating, so a diagnostic can never condemn a worker).

selection_direct.note: THE DIRECT HALF of selection_honored, and it does not replace the output-comparison half — both are reported, because they answer different questions and disagreement between them is itself informative. The gate's own selection_honored check concludes the right object was loaded because the output looks like that arm's output; that inference is sound only while outputs are composition-stable, which is what VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 was providing. This half instead reads the worker's OWN record of which object it resolved and bound for each request, so it holds at either BI setting. Read the pair together: direct passes and output fails = the right objects were loaded and the outputs moved for numerical reasons (expected at BI=0); direct FAILS = a real routing bug, which outranks everything else in this record; both pass = the strongest form of the claim. The worker record ships its own `coverage` string stating what it does not cover — notably op-level mis-binding downstream of selection, which would read as a clean pass here. If it does not hold, every selected row comes back `unobserved` and the verdict is MISSING — never a pass — while the AGGREGATE half (every observation the worker made bound what was asked for, plus the set of cells actually resolved) still applies, because it needs no correlation at all.
